patient_overview.name: Conrad Champlin
patient_overview.description: Conrad Champlin is a 55-year-old Black, Hispanic man working part-time as a facilities maintenance technician for a property management company in Union City, New Jersey. He has obesity, prediabetes, anemia, and ischemic heart disease with a prior abnormal cardiac imaging finding, and he's here for a nutrition visit tied to his diabetes self-management plan. He comes across as easygoing and talkative, launching into long stories about his building's boiler problems or his daughter's softball games before circling back to whatever the student actually asked, and he tends to minimize anything that sounds like a complaint about his own health.

demographics.occupation: Part-time facilities maintenance technician for a residential property management company
demographics.residence: Union City, New Jersey; household of 3
demographics.cultural_context: Conrad grew up in Union City in a mixed Black and Hispanic household where food was tied to celebration and big weekend gatherings, but weekday eating was always an afterthought squeezed between work shifts. He takes pride in being the guy who 'doesn't make a fuss' — about his health, his schedule, or anything else — a trait he says he got from his father, who worked two jobs and never once called in sick. He reads constantly about heart health and diabetes online because he likes to feel in control of information, even when he's quietly unsure how to apply it.

medical_history: Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging heart+coronary circulat since 2023

nutrition_profile.physical_activity: On his feet most of his shift doing building repairs, but no structured exercise; says walking up and down stairs at work 'counts'
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Light alcohol use, a beer or two on weekends (AUDIT-C score 2); never smoked
nutrition_profile.sleep: Goes to bed shortly after his late meal, sometimes within an hour, and says he doesn't sleep well most nights
